newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Next profits up 27 pct, shares slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Next profits up 27 pct, shares slip.

text.p: British fashion chain Next Plc on Wednesday unveiled a sharp rise in first half profits, but its shares fell on fears that current sales may have lagged an upturn in consumer spending.
Pretax profits in the first half were nearly 27 percent higher at 56 million pounds ($87.11 million) and at the top of market expectations.
But disappointment with sales growth in the second half dampened enthusiasm for the results and hit the shares, which fell 23.5 pence to 576.5 pence.

Next stores saw sales rise by 23 percent on selling space that was five percent up on the previous year. Next Directory, the mail order business, boosted sales by 23 percent and operating profit by 42 percent.
Total sales sales rose to 406.4 million pounds from 333.3 million. The dividend was increased by a hefty 33 percent to 5.0 pence from 3.75 pence.

Next said sales in its stores were 14 percent higher than the previous year in the five weeks from August 12. But this was inflated by a five percent increase in selling space. Mail order sales were 20 percent higher in the same period.
Retail analysts said the second half sales increase was slower than expected.
"The increase in sales is a lot slower than people were expecting," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at MeesPierson.
He said the market had expected Next to receive a bigger boost from Britain's hot summer.
Chairman Lord Wolfson said in a statement the results showed the Next brand was still making good progress in retailing and home shopping.
The group's mail order business Next Directory saw an 18 percent rise in customers to 620,000 in the half year.
Chief executive David Jones said, "We're really quite pleased with our growth in customers."

Jones said in an interview Next was quite relaxed about its 143 million pound cash mountain, which it would use to fund its generous dividend payouts and also for investment in its warehouse reorganisation, due for completion by end 1997.
"We don't have to go running to banks to do what we want to do," he said, "We don't feel embarrassed by having 140 odd million."
Jones dismissed speculation that the appointment of Next chairman Lord Wolfson as chairman of Great Universal Stores Plc might lead to a link-up between the two retailers.
"I don't really think that there's anything on the horizon at the moment, not as far as I'm aware."
Next recently rejoined Britain's FTSE index of top 100 companies. It was a high flier in the 1980s retail boom but overexpansion brought the group almost to its knees five years ago. ($1=.6428 Pound)
